topic.angle: Pale moths turned dark with soot, then pale again

panels.text: Before the Industrial Revolution, peppered moths in England were mostly pale. Pale wings were nearly invisible against light, lichen-covered bark, and the black form was rare.
Then coal-burning factories blanketed the countryside with soot. Many lichens died and the trees darkened, so birds found pale moths more easily.
Dark moths now survived more often and passed their colour on. By 1895, the dark form had reached a reported 98% of moths in Manchester.
The twist: from about 1962, as the air got cleaner, the dark form steadily declined. The moths did not choose anything. Whichever colour hid better simply left more offspring.

probes.question: Why did dark peppered moths become common near industrial cities?
options: They chose darker trees to rest on
Soot darkened the trees, so dark moths were eaten less often and left more offspring
Pollution turned each moth's wings dark

probes.question: True or false: the dark form of the peppered moth declined again from about 1962 as the air became cleaner.

claims.claim: Before the Industrial Revolution the black form was rare and pale moths blended with light lichen-covered bark
claims.quote: The light-bodied moths were able to blend in with the light-coloured lichens and tree bark, and the less common black moths were more likely to be eaten by birds.

claims.claim: Coal soot covered the countryside, many lichens died, trees darkened, so birds found pale moths more easily
claims.quote: Many of the light-bodied lichens died from sulphur dioxide emissions, and the trees became darkened.

claims.claim: Dark moths survived more often and passed colour on; birds eat the less camouflaged form (probe 1 answer)
claims.quote: As a result, birds would find and eat those morphs that were not camouflaged with increased frequency.

claims.claim: By 1895 the dark form reached a reported 98% in Manchester
claims.quote: By 1895, it had reached a reported frequency of 98% in Manchester.

claims.claim: From about 1962 the dark form steadily declined as the air got cleaner (body and probe 2)
claims.quote: From around 1962 to the present, the phenotype frequency of carbonaria has steadily fallen in line with cleaner air around industrial cities.

claims.claim: Moths did not choose; whichever colour hid better left more offspring (natural selection)
claims.quote: Natural selection is the differential survival and reproduction of individuals due to differences in the relative fitness endowed on them by their own particular complement of observable characteristics.
